findings.description: The instance's user_data embeds a plaintext AWS access key ID and secret access key (AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA / wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMAAAKEY). User data is retrievable via instance metadata and the EC2 API, so the keys are exposed to anyone who can query the instance, and any IAM permissions bound to that principal are effectively public.
Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the publicly addressed instance to brute-force and exploitation attempts from the entire internet. This is a genuine finding.
The EBS volume has no encrypted attribute, so the Terraform default leaves the disk unencrypted at rest. This is a genuine finding.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0. Combined with public IP assignment, this exposes the web service to untrusted networks without restriction or mediation. Genuine but of limited added risk for a public web portal.

map_public_ip_on_launch is true on the subnet hosting the portal server, ensuring the instance is directly reachable from the internet in combination with the permissive security group. Genuine finding.

The egress rule permits all protocols and all ports to 0.0.0.0/0, removing outbound network boundaries and enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised instance. Genuine, low-to-medium impact given the instance already has broad outbound needs.

The snapshot does not specify encryption and is taken from the unencrypted volume, so the point-in-time copy is stored unencrypted. Genuine, though it is a direct consequence of the unencrypted source volume.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so every instance launched in this subnet receives a publicly routable IPv4 address by default. Genuine finding.
The bucket that stores VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving traffic metadata stored in cleartext. Genuine finding.

findings.issue_category: public access not blocked and force_destroy enabled
findings.description: The netflow archive bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so account-level defaults are the only protection; force_destroy = true also permits the bucket and its log data to be deleted by any principal with s3:DeleteBucket without confirmation. Log data destruction defeats the audit trail.

findings.issue_category: IAM credentials embedded in provisioning script
findings.description: Instance user_data also exports AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and the access keys, meaning that if any IAM policy is attached to the instance profile the long-lived static keys are the effective identity. No aws_iam_instance_profile is defined here, so the embedded keys are the sole credential and cannot be scoped or rotated by IAM; treat as part of the same hard-coded credential exposure.
